changed.what: Applied F-U24a-1's request, checked against BD-201, BD-253 and BD-368 (each records its part with --part). The script now writes only the receipt. Each milestone part of GATE-ARENA-01 is recorded outside any script with record_gate --part <milestone> by its one recording bead (BD-201 M2, BD-253 M3, BD-368 M4). The M1 referee rows come from N24c-07's arena_m1_families.sh. Applied F-U24c's request: dep N24cp3-01 (eval.run on batched tiers; no cycle). The negative controls are now rows of controls.toml, run through e2e_expect_caught and planted with --features gauntlet-mutations plus the control's feature (BD-025, N38b-04). Left as it was: the script would write gate rows (convention 9), and its eval run --tier batch-cpu would call a tier its dependencies do not deliver.

Added dep N24cp3-01. The script runs eval run --tier batch-cpu, which only N24cp3-01 delivers, and no path reached it (convention 8; no cycle). Left as it was: the bead could start before the batched eval tier exists, and its script could not run.

The ramp bracket said 0.26 fails and 0.27 passes. But μ* = 0.2628 puts 0.26 inside the referee's 0.005 exclusion band (0.0028 away; BD-123's grid rule). The referee bracket is now 0.25 (fails) and 0.27 (passes), the fast-tier bracket 0.25 and 0.28, plus one boundary-flagged run at μ*. The acceptance criterion matches. No M3 run input sets friction, so the rig command now names one design file per grid point, generated from a template, and carries --task, --worlds 1, --seconds and a distinct --key per μ. Left as it was: the known answer asserted a point the grid excludes, and the command could not vary μ.

The rig commands now name the design file of each case: the stopping rig at μ_b of water and of oil, and the film rig at its three cases. A run command has no load, radius or film input at M3. Left as it was: the script could not produce the cases it asserts.

Added the near-boundary labelled examples that admission rule 3 of N24a-12 requires: each comparator within a tenth of its scale (i_ratio in (0.99, 1], pitch in [40.5°, 45°), slide-back between 0.18 and 0.20 m), a synthetic fallback, and no-strike shown both ways. The rig command now runs a design file per grid point with --task, --tier, --seed and a distinct --key. Left as it was: admission would refuse the family with FROB-REF-539, and its rig runs would share receipts.

The ee example ('stops 0.025 m from the grasp frame') now states that it fails ee-at-tote with margin −0.25. Added rule 3's near-boundary set: 0.019 m; tote tilt in [9°, 10°); tip margin ≤ 5 mm; base tilt in [13.5°, 15°); clearance ≤ 3 mm; synthetic fallback. The tip-rig and attachment-card commands now carry --task, --scene, --tier, --seed and distinct keys. Left as it was: refusal 539 at admission, and runs that a test compares sharing one receipt.

Applied the scene.split request (NJL-01 action rule): create is the default call, add is --action add, and each has its own --key. Added the required --scenes to frob train start (N23a-14). Removed a deadlock: BD-259 (eval.qualify) depends on this bead through BD-255 → BD-253, so this bead cannot test qualify's 502. Its acceptance criterion and the training_side_label test now cover eval.compare and eval.promote. Qualify's planted 502 is BD-259's refusals_before_commit_match_registry. Left as it was: positional action words are refused with 802, train start without --scenes is refused, and the bead could never close.

Applied H-owners-3 and M1-4: eval.ledger's admin actions are --action open|close and take no key (--key is 802). The three command lines now read frob eval ledger --action open … and frob eval ledger <campaign> --action close --json. Added two deps (both M3, no cycle). BD-261 delivers qual:admin, the 720 of the stop-and-restart strategy. N24b-19 delivers FROB-REF-845, the code of the launder strategy. The acceptance criterion requires the real lane to refuse all six strategies with their codes, and the bead reached neither. Left as it was: the self-check script would stop at 802 on its first ledger call, and two of the six refusals had no delivering dependency.

Applied H-verbs-9. The Scope no longer calls FROB-REF-896 a chapter refusal of the verb. The verb reaches it only as the cause of the surface's appended 806 (N29-REF surfaces_as), and it is not in the row's list (VERBS-telemetry lists 883, 888 and 898). Left as it was: an implementer would raise 896 from the verb or put it on the row, against the registry.

Took this bead's side of the audit proposal for N29b-01. Checked: this bead runs energy_ledger_referee.sh, with N29b-01's step groups, to a pass; N24b-03 is M1 and does not reach this bead. The bead now registers, with N24b-03's manifest, the three fixtures that the breakdown-*, bus-* and pertask-* step groups run through frob sim run --fixture, and it depends on N24b-03 directly. Left as it was: once N29b-01 drops that registration, no bead would register the fixtures and those step groups could not run.

Applied F-U29b's request. The seven wave-1 classes become rows of fixtures/e2e/chron08/list.toml with wave = 1, as 64-world batches with 8 planted addresses like N29b-05's rows. The tier step is now a stage that runs scripts/e2e/gate_chron_08.sh, which exports FROB_CHRON08_REFEREE. A session that did not implement the monitors re-records the gate's one part from that receipt with record_gate … --part M2 (new section 7 and acceptance line). Added dep N29b-06 (its list and its script; M2, no cycle), as the sibling wave beads N22ap2-03, BD-394 and N19b-13 have. Removed the C13 narration 'requested of N29b-06'. The wave numbering now matches N29b-06's table: 2 gait-instability, 3 model-drift, 4 slosh-tip. Left as it was: the bare cargo line fails the referee-rows entry, so wave 1 could never be recorded.

Applied F-U24a-1's request: stage failures-stage runs BD-094's telemetry_failures.sh. Applied F-U29b's request: the referee receipt is a canonical JSON file named by the BLAKE3 hash of its bytes, written under target/e2e-receipts/telemetry_verbs/ with its hash and path logged. Its fields are commit, seeds, thirteen class rows {class, fixture, expected_tick, measured_tick, pass} and the two accounting assertions with pass. The reference to N29b-06's old step record is gone, and a new unit test, referee_receipt_canonical, covers the receipt. Took the audit counterpart from N24a-44: the extremum-* group asserts kind, sense (max, max, min) and coverage, with an acceptance line. Found: setup ran frob sim run with no fixture, seed or telemetry level. The fixtures are now registered conformance fixtures, run with --fixture <space>/<name> --telemetry T2 --seed --key. At the default level T1 no traces are kept, so --traced-worlds would return the empty set and the query, energy and extremum groups would fail. The controls are now controls.toml rows, planted with gauntlet-mutations plus their nc feature and run through e2e_expect_caught.

Applied H-verbs-9's request: the row lists 731, 840 and 888 (detail still-collected); the sentence '888 is requested of it' is gone (convention 13). Also, FROB-REF-840 was given exit 3, while N24-REF's row (and BD-261, N28a-17, N28a-21) give exit 5. Now exit 5, and sealed_refused_840 asserts it. Left as it was: the implementer would return the wrong exit for a sealed still, and the agent would retry a capability refusal as a bad input.

Applied F-U37's request: the M2 handler's export checks now run in the export door's order (N37-18): flags 816, privacy 731, licence 733, then the path 734. The M3 switch to export::admit therefore changes no answer. Applied H-ref-3's request: 'FROB-REF-836/-837 (provisional number)' is replaced by the held ledger slugs packet-over-byte-cap and packet-frames-not-retained, raised behind REFUSAL_PACKET_OVER_BYTE_CAP and REFUSAL_PACKET_FRAMES_NOT_RETAINED, with exit 3 and no interim code. over_cap_is_836_exit_3 becomes over_cap_is_slug_exit_3, and the tests assert the slug and exit 3. Left as it was: tests would assert numbers that N35x-01 holds, and the M2 order would differ from the door's.

Applied F-U24c's requests. The unregistered task.verdict options were already gone. planted_table_complete now reads gates::arena::GATE_ARENA_03_REFUSALS (N24c-06), and the Considerations state N24c-06's files_of_record_complete as a fact, where they said 'is asked to' (C13). Applied H-verbs-8: dep N16ap4-01 (sim.run --task at M1; no cycle). Applied F-U24a-1's overlay item in the owner's current form: the two planted overlays are frob.task.overlay/1 documents carrying the schema member by which a .json file is routed (N24a-13). Found: step 6 called task verdict --requirement dwell, but --requirement names a verdict (N24c-02) and dwell is an online signal. KA-596 now runs as its Gauntlet row. The controls are now controls.toml rows built with gauntlet-mutations and run through e2e_expect_caught. Not applied: F-U24a-1's request to run the spec beads' own scripts as stages. The owners (N24a-02, -03, -04, -05, -07, -08, -13), revised in this round, now state that this script does not run theirs and that its one stage is BD-121's. Applying the request would contradict seven owners, and both forms satisfy convention 11.

The e2e ran three μ values through one compiled rig with no friction input, so the three runs were the same run under three keys, and the 'μ ∈ {0.3, 0.5, 0.8}' check passed vacuously. The rig is now compiled once per μ, and each run passes --scene with the design positional. Each compile is followed by e2e_scene_ready, and dep BD-228 is added (M3, no cycle). From M3 a run on a pack with an incomplete acceptance report is FROB-REF-318, and the lint scene-ready-before-run fails the script. The planted control is now --features gauntlet-mutations,frob-contact/planted-no-belt-work, a controls.toml row, where it was a loose 'test build flag'. Left as it was: the friction sweep proved nothing, and every run would be refused from M3.

Applied the audit proposal after checking it. The acceptance item 'frob telemetry query returns the kind, sense and coverage' was this bead's only use of N24a-36, and its e2e steps belong to N24a-39. N24a-06 to N24a-10 reached N24a-36 only through this bead, and none of them calls telemetry.query itself. The item moved to N24a-39's extremum-* group (named in an acceptance line here), and N24a-36 moved from deps to related. Left as it was: the extremum kind waited on the query verb for no work it does.

Section 2 said every run carries an explicit seed. eval.run's battery form takes none (--run-seed beside --battery is 802), so the rule now applies only to verbs that take a seed. The metrics-core step now names its calls: eval run --battery … --key, then eval scorecard , which had no run to score, and eval scorecard --quantile 0.99. The controls are now controls.toml rows planted with gauntlet-mutations through e2e_expect_caught; three of them are N24a-22's nc rows. Request part checked: eval.scorecard's row now lists --quantile

, so that call stands. Not applied: running arena_metrics_core.sh, arena_metrics_energy.sh and arena_scorecard_table.sh as stages. The owners N24a-17, -18 and -22, revised in this round, now say this script does not run theirs. Left as it was: a seeded eval run is refused with 802, and the scorecard call is malformed.

Left as it was: an implementer would wait on a registry change that has already been made.

The format row for group-element was 'requested of N34-09' (C13), and N34-09 never added it. VERBS-task's task.check already carries element = artifact-input<group-element>. This bead now enters the row itself through N34-19's registry (DESIGN id FMT-GROUP-ELEMENT, schema frob.group.element/1, .json routed by its schema member, owner frob-spec, reader rep::read_element, decision N34-27's record), as N24a-13 does for the overlay format. The acceptance criterion and core_classification_table required the maneuver-cost and fallback-count records. Those are N24a-21's (M3), and this bead is M2. The bead now writes smoothness into every record present at M2 (N24a-17 to N24a-20). The two M3 rows are the rule N24a-21 follows and join the test when registered. Left as it was: the bead could not close until a later milestone.

requests.what: As the audit proposed, N24a-37 now registers the three step-group fixtures with N24b-03's manifest (reference quadruped trotting, two-joint braking, two-design per-task) and depends on N24b-03. Drop the clause 'the fixtures are registered with N24b-03's manifest' and the dep N24b-03, or say if you keep them, so the fixtures have one owner. Otherwise two beads register the same three fixtures.

N24a-39's fixtures are now registered conformance fixtures under crates/frob-conformance/fixtures/<space>/<name>; frob sim run --fixture resolves only those and assets/fixtures/<name>, and --scene arrives at M2. Move fail/brownout-exhausted and fail/brownout-ceiling there, register them, and run them as frob sim run --fixture fail/brownout-exhausted --tier referee --telemetry T2 --seed 3 --key <k> --json. The positional fail/... is read as a design path, and the runs have no --key, so the failures-brownout-* steps cannot run as written.

N24ax-04's loader rule refuses a metric record without smoothness, and its table fixes your two records: maneuver cost smooth-accumulation (smooth_in design-continuous) and fallback count count. Register them with those values and add dep N24ax-04 (M2; no cycle). Otherwise your M3 records fail the registry load.
